_doc: Store-ops parameters. Every entry: value, unit, range, source (URL/paper or 'assumption: why'), confidence (high = measured, peer-reviewed or official; medium = measured but small/old/US; low = labelled assumption). Built 2026-10-03 from fetched sources; see data/ops/evidence.md for quotes.

staffed_fixed_s.source: Klee, E. (2006) 'Paper or Plastic? The Effect of Time on Check and Debit Card Use at Grocery Stores', Federal Reserve FEDS 2006-02, Table 3(a) and Section A, https://www.federalreserve.gov/pubs/feds/2006/200602/200602pap.pdf (US grocery chain scanner data, 24,354 transactions; 'ring time' = first item scanned to cashier drawer close): intercept of ring-time regression, debit-card payers (42.997, SE 1.4); check payers 75.061.
staffed_fixed_s.note: US data, 1990s-2000s tender mix. Card payment is the modern UK default, so the debit intercept is used. Excludes queueing and customer unload time.

staffed_per_item_s.source: Klee, E. (2006) 'Paper or Plastic? The Effect of Time on Check and Debit Card Use at Grocery Stores', Federal Reserve FEDS 2006-02, Table 3(a) and Section A, https://www.federalreserve.gov/pubs/feds/2006/200602/200602pap.pdf (US grocery chain scanner data, 24,354 transactions; 'ring time' = first item scanned to cashier drawer close): items-bought coefficient 3.242 (debit), 3.775 (check); squared term -0.001 (n.s.). Range low end: Edwards, J. & Kenner, R. (2004) 'The Effectiveness of Self-Checkout', Worcester Polytechnic Institute IQP 04D068I, Table 13 'Experiential study time results' (timed purchases at Home Depot, Wal-Mart, BJ's, Price Chopper), http://digital.wpi.edu/downloads/8049g5702 cashier unit scan time 2-3 s/item.
staffed_per_item_s.note: Includes cashier scanning and bagging as practised in the sample stores.

staffed_mean_ring_time_by_tender_s.source: Klee, E. (2006) 'Paper or Plastic? The Effect of Time on Check and Debit Card Use at Grocery Stores', Federal Reserve FEDS 2006-02, Table 3(a) and Section A, https://www.federalreserve.gov/pubs/feds/2006/200602/200602pap.pdf (US grocery chain scanner data, 24,354 transactions; 'ring time' = first item scanned to cashier drawer close) Section A (means over all baskets).

basket_items_median_us.source: Klee, E. (2006) 'Paper or Plastic? The Effect of Time on Check and Debit Card Use at Grocery Stores', Federal Reserve FEDS 2006-02, Table 3(a) and Section A, https://www.federalreserve.gov/pubs/feds/2006/200602/200602pap.pdf (US grocery chain scanner data, 24,354 transactions; 'ring time' = first item scanned to cashier drawer close) Table 2 summary: median ~12, mean 16.66 items; ring time median 109 s, mean 128 s, top-coded 600 s.
basket_items_median_us.note: Right-skewed; use for sanity checks of the mission-weighted basket mix.

basket_items_mean_us.source: Klee, E. (2006) 'Paper or Plastic? The Effect of Time on Check and Debit Card Use at Grocery Stores', Federal Reserve FEDS 2006-02, Table 3(a) and Section A, https://www.federalreserve.gov/pubs/feds/2006/200602/200602pap.pdf (US grocery chain scanner data, 24,354 transactions; 'ring time' = first item scanned to cashier drawer close)

sco_initiation_s.source: Edwards, J. & Kenner, R. (2004) 'The Effectiveness of Self-Checkout', Worcester Polytechnic Institute IQP 04D068I, Table 13 'Experiential study time results' (timed purchases at Home Depot, Wal-Mart, BJ's, Price Chopper), http://digital.wpi.edu/downloads/8049g5702: 'Initiation Time' 5/5/5/15 s across 4 stores, mean 7.5.

sco_per_item_s.source: Edwards, J. & Kenner, R. (2004) 'The Effectiveness of Self-Checkout', Worcester Polytechnic Institute IQP 04D068I, Table 13 'Experiential study time results' (timed purchases at Home Depot, Wal-Mart, BJ's, Price Chopper), http://digital.wpi.edu/downloads/8049g5702: ACM 'Unit Scan Time' 5/6/5/8 s; mean 6.0. Same study's cashier unit scan time 2-3 s, so SCO is ~2.2x slower per item.
sco_per_item_s.note: 2004 hardware; modern SCO probably at the faster end. Ratio to staffed (2.2x) is the more robust quantity.

sco_payment_card_s.source: Edwards, J. & Kenner, R. (2004) 'The Effectiveness of Self-Checkout', Worcester Polytechnic Institute IQP 04D068I, Table 13 'Experiential study time results' (timed purchases at Home Depot, Wal-Mart, BJ's, Price Chopper), http://digital.wpi.edu/downloads/8049g5702: ACM 'Transaction Time, Credit' 20/30/20/25 s.

sco_payment_cash_s.source: Edwards, J. & Kenner, R. (2004) 'The Effectiveness of Self-Checkout', Worcester Polytechnic Institute IQP 04D068I, Table 13 'Experiential study time results' (timed purchases at Home Depot, Wal-Mart, BJ's, Price Chopper), http://digital.wpi.edu/downloads/8049g5702: ACM 'Transaction Time, Cash' 30/35/30/40 s.

staffed_payment_card_s.source: Edwards, J. & Kenner, R. (2004) 'The Effectiveness of Self-Checkout', Worcester Polytechnic Institute IQP 04D068I, Table 13 'Experiential study time results' (timed purchases at Home Depot, Wal-Mart, BJ's, Price Chopper), http://digital.wpi.edu/downloads/8049g5702: standard checkout 'Transaction Time, Credit' 20/33.3/20/20 s.
staffed_payment_card_s.note: Already inside staffed_fixed_s; listed for the breakdown only.

sco_deactivation_s.source: Edwards, J. & Kenner, R. (2004) 'The Effectiveness of Self-Checkout', Worcester Polytechnic Institute IQP 04D068I, Table 13 'Experiential study time results' (timed purchases at Home Depot, Wal-Mart, BJ's, Price Chopper), http://digital.wpi.edu/downloads/8049g5702: 'Deactivation Time' 2/5/0/3 s.

sco_intervention_prob.source: Edwards, J. & Kenner, R. (2004) 'The Effectiveness of Self-Checkout', Worcester Polytechnic Institute IQP 04D068I, Table 13 'Experiential study time results' (timed purchases at Home Depot, Wal-Mart, BJ's, Price Chopper), http://digital.wpi.edu/downloads/8049g5702: 'Problem Frequency' 25/30/20/60 % of SCO transactions; mean 33.75%.
sco_intervention_prob.note: 2004 machines; no newer public measured rate fetched. An industry vendor paper (CARI J. Tech. Sci. 2026, doi:10.47941/jts.3523) cites 18-25% false-positive alerts, consistent with the low end.

sco_intervention_resolution_s.source: Edwards, J. & Kenner, R. (2004) 'The Effectiveness of Self-Checkout', Worcester Polytechnic Institute IQP 04D068I, Table 13 'Experiential study time results' (timed purchases at Home Depot, Wal-Mart, BJ's, Price Chopper), http://digital.wpi.edu/downloads/8049g5702: 'Problem Resolution Time' 40/30/45/60 s; text: missing staff 'may add between 1 and 5 minutes'.

sco_terminals_per_attendant.source: Wikipedia 'Self-checkout' https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-checkout: 'one attendant can often run four to six checkout lanes'.

scan_only_speedup.source: 'Automation-Enabled Specialization and Retail Service Productivity' (2024), doi:10.66033/jmpr2024-111 (abstract via OpenAlex): within-cashier field experiment, 4 Singapore supermarket outlets, 152,246 transactions, 38 cashiers: scan-only counters raised scanning speed 10.9% and customer service rate ~21%.
scan_only_speedup.note: Use for an express / scan-only staffed lane variant.

produce_weigh_s_staffed.source: assumption: cashier keys a PLU from memory and the scale is in the scanner bed; set ~1 item-time (3.24 s, staffed_per_item_s) rounded up. No measured source fetched.

produce_weigh_s_sco.source: assumption: shopper searches the touchscreen produce menu; range upper bound 40 s is Edwards, J. & Kenner, R. (2004) 'The Effectiveness of Self-Checkout', Worcester Polytechnic Institute IQP 04D068I, Table 13 'Experiential study time results' (timed purchases at Home Depot, Wal-Mart, BJ's, Price Chopper), http://digital.wpi.edu/downloads/8049g5702 ('items without bar codes ... adds about 40 sec for each item' when assistance is needed).

age_check_delay_s_sco.unit: s per transaction with an age-restricted item
age_check_delay_s_sco.source: assumption: an age-restricted item forces an attendant approval, modelled as one SCO intervention (sco_intervention_resolution_s, Edwards, J. & Kenner, R. (2004) 'The Effectiveness of Self-Checkout', Worcester Polytechnic Institute IQP 04D068I, Table 13 'Experiential study time results' (timed purchases at Home Depot, Wal-Mart, BJ's, Price Chopper), http://digital.wpi.edu/downloads/8049g5702). UK Challenge 25 practice means most alcohol baskets trigger it.

age_check_delay_s_staffed.unit: s per transaction with an age-restricted item
age_check_delay_s_staffed.source: assumption: cashier glances / asks for ID in-lane; 30 s upper bound when ID is requested and inspected. No measured source fetched.

value.sco: sco_initiation_s + sco_per_item_s*n_items + sco_payment_card_s + sco_deactivation_s + produce_weigh_s_sco*n_loose + age_check_delay_s_sco*has_age_item + sco_intervention_prob*sco_intervention_resolution_s

service_time_formula.source: Additive model: staffed slope/intercept from Klee 2006 Table 3(a); SCO components from WPI 2004 Table 13. Klee finds the items effect is near-linear (squared term -0.001, n.s. for debit).

weekday_shopping_trip_start_share_by_hou.unit: fraction of weekday shopping trips starting in hour h (index 0 = 00:00-00:59)
weekday_shopping_trip_start_share_by_hou.source: DfT National Travel Survey 2025, NTS0502b 'Trip purpose by trip start time (Monday to Friday only): England', row 'Shopping' (unweighted sample 35,864 trips), https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/6a9ecdd5474b8101ece46434/nts0502.ods
weekday_shopping_trip_start_share_by_hou.note: Covers all shopping trips (not only grocery) and is trip START time; arrival at store is later by the trip duration. Peak 11:00-11:59 (13.0%); 10:00-14:59 holds 54.5%. Weekends not in this table: reuse the weekday curve (assumption).

shopping_trips_by_day_share.source: DfT NTS 2025, NTS0504b 'day_purpose', column 'Shopping' (trips per person per year: Mon 20.0, Tue 18.2, Wed 17.6, Thu 18.5, Fri 22.0, Sat 30.1, Sun 19.0), https://www.gov.uk/government/statistical-data-sets/nts05-trips (table NTS0504b_day_purpose)

shopping_trips_day_multiplier.note: Saturday is 1.45x an average day. Sunday trading hours are capped at 6 h for large stores in England & Wales (Sunday Trading Act 1994), so Sunday's trips are compressed into fewer hours.

school_escort_trip_start_share_15h.unit: fraction of weekday 'escort education' trips starting 15:00-15:59
school_escort_trip_start_share_15h.note: Grounds the after-school family-shop window at ~15:00-17:00.

commute_trip_start_share_17h.unit: fraction of weekday commuting trips starting 17:00-17:59
commute_trip_start_share_17h.note: Grounds the after-work top-up window at ~17:00-19:00.

store_customers_per_week.source: Gruen, T. & Corsten, D. (2008) 'A Comprehensive Guide to Retail Out-of-Stock Reduction in the FMCG Industry', GMA/FMI/NACDS/P&G, https://www.nacds.org/pdfs/membership/out_of_stock.pdf, cost example table: 'Avg # customers/week 10,900' (supermarket, avg transaction $27.34) vs 4,000 (smaller format).
store_customers_per_week.note: US illustrative store; used only to scale absolute arrivals.

peak_arrivals_per_hour_example.note: Applies the weekday hour curve to Saturday (assumption).

arrival_process.source: assumption: standard for independent shoppers in queueing models (M/M/c / Erlang C); rate per hour = weekly volume * day share * hour share. No UK test of Poisson-ness fetched.

trip_start_to_arrival_lag_min.source: assumption: typical local shopping trip duration; shifts the NTS start-time curve to store arrivals. No NTS value fetched for shopping trip duration.

mission_mix_by_daypart.source: assumption: windows anchored on sourced peaks (NTS shopping peak 10-14h; school-escort peak 15h; commute-home peak 17h) but the mission shares themselves are not sourced. IGD/Kantar mission data not fetchable (research/04 notes 404).

after_school_treat_uplift.unit: x treat/dessert mission share vs baseline
after_school_treat_uplift.source: assumption: family trips after the 15:00 school pick-up (NTS escort peak) carry more snacks/desserts. No daypart category-share source found; set 1.0 to switch off.

basket_items_by_mission.source: meal_deal/top_up/weekly_shop: research/04-3d-sim-evidence-and-tech.md section 1 'UK meal-deal and missions' (labelled [M] assumptions there; IGD/Kantar 404); meal deal = main+snack+drink (Reddit r/CasualUK 1bc79kh, research/corpus/meal_deal.md). treat and gym: assumption. Sanity check vs Klee, E. (2006) 'Paper or Plastic? The Effect of Time on Check and Debit Card Use at Grocery Stores', Federal Reserve FEDS 2006-02, Table 3(a) and Section A, https://www.federalreserve.gov/pubs/feds/2006/200602/200602pap.pdf (US grocery chain scanner data, 24,354 transactions; 'ring time' = first item scanned to cashier drawer close) all-transaction median 12 / mean 16.7.

basket_size_distribution.source: assumption: count data that is right-skewed like Klee's (mean 16.7 > median 12).

oos_rate.unit: fraction of SKU-store observations out of stock
oos_rate.source: Gruen, Corsten & Bharadwaj (2002) 'Retail Out-of-Stocks: A Worldwide Examination of Extent, Causes and Consumer Responses', GMA; figures as summarised in Gruen, T. & Corsten, D. (2008) 'A Comprehensive Guide to Retail Out-of-Stock Reduction in the FMCG Industry', GMA/FMI/NACDS/P&G, https://www.nacds.org/pdfs/membership/out_of_stock.pdf and research/04-3d-sim-evidence-and-tech.md row 21 [V]. Range: Gruen 2007 regional figures quoted in 'The Effect of Inventory Level on Product Availability and Sale', Prague Economic Papers 2015, doi:10.18267/j.pep.556, https://pep.vse.cz/doi/10.18267/j.pep.556.pdf (quoting Gruen 2007 regional OOS rates): north-west Europe 7.2%, south/east Europe 10.8%, Europe 8.6%, US 7.9%.

oos_reaction.unit: share of shoppers facing an OOS
oos_reaction.source: Gruen, Corsten & Bharadwaj (2002) 'Retail Out-of-Stocks: A Worldwide Examination of Extent, Causes and Consumer Responses', GMA; figures as summarised in Gruen, T. & Corsten, D. (2008) 'A Comprehensive Guide to Retail Out-of-Stock Reduction in the FMCG Industry', GMA/FMI/NACDS/P&G, https://www.nacds.org/pdfs/membership/out_of_stock.pdf and research/04-3d-sim-evidence-and-tech.md row 21 [V] (71,000+ consumers)

oos_root_cause.source: Gruen, T. & Corsten, D. (2008) 'A Comprehensive Guide to Retail Out-of-Stock Reduction in the FMCG Industry', GMA/FMI/NACDS/P&G, https://www.nacds.org/pdfs/membership/out_of_stock.pdf (root-cause pie in executive summary; 2002 study: ~75% store practices)
oos_root_cause.note: Restockers address the 25% shelf share; manager ordering addresses the 47%.

shoppers_encountering_oos.unit: fraction of shoppers meeting >=1 OOS per trip
shoppers_encountering_oos.source: Gruen, T. & Corsten, D. (2008) 'A Comprehensive Guide to Retail Out-of-Stock Reduction in the FMCG Industry', GMA/FMI/NACDS/P&G, https://www.nacds.org/pdfs/membership/out_of_stock.pdf cost table

oos_staff_query_prob.unit: fraction of OOS-hit shoppers who ask staff
oos_staff_query_prob.source: Gruen, T. & Corsten, D. (2008) 'A Comprehensive Guide to Retail Out-of-Stock Reduction in the FMCG Industry', GMA/FMI/NACDS/P&G, https://www.nacds.org/pdfs/membership/out_of_stock.pdf cost table ('% times shoppers involve store labor 10%')

oos_staff_query_min.source: Gruen, T. & Corsten, D. (2008) 'A Comprehensive Guide to Retail Out-of-Stock Reduction in the FMCG Industry', GMA/FMI/NACDS/P&G, https://www.nacds.org/pdfs/membership/out_of_stock.pdf cost table (6 min supermarket, 4 min small format)

oos_weekend_effect.source: Gruen, T. & Corsten, D. (2008) 'A Comprehensive Guide to Retail Out-of-Stock Reduction in the FMCG Industry', GMA/FMI/NACDS/P&G, https://www.nacds.org/pdfs/membership/out_of_stock.pdf ch.2-3: 'knowing that OOS will increase on Saturday and Sunday, stocking labor can be reallocated'

retail_sales_lost_to_oos.source: Gruen, T. & Corsten, D. (2008) 'A Comprehensive Guide to Retail Out-of-Stock Reduction in the FMCG Industry', GMA/FMI/NACDS/P&G, https://www.nacds.org/pdfs/membership/out_of_stock.pdf exec summary (from 2002 study)

instore_logistics_share_of_staff_hours.source: Reiner, G., Teller, C. & Kotzab, H. (2013) 'Analyzing the Efficient Execution of In-Store Logistics Processes in Grocery Retailing: The Case of Dairy Products', Production and Operations Management 22(4), doi:10.1111/poms.12003; survey of 202 stores of one central-European chain; green OA copy https://openresearch.surrey.ac.uk/view/delivery/44SUR_INST/12138884720002346/13140556810002346 (Table 3) citing Liebmann & Zentes 2001: in-store logistics 'can take up more than 40% of the working hours of store employees'

dairy_shelf_replenishment_hours_per_day.source: Reiner, G., Teller, C. & Kotzab, H. (2013) 'Analyzing the Efficient Execution of In-Store Logistics Processes in Grocery Retailing: The Case of Dairy Products', Production and Operations Management 22(4), doi:10.1111/poms.12003; survey of 202 stores of one central-European chain; green OA copy https://openresearch.surrey.ac.uk/view/delivery/44SUR_INST/12138884720002346/13140556810002346 (Table 3) Table 3 'Time for shelf replenishment'; staff-hours 4.1/8.8/14.3

restock_cases_per_hour.source: assumption: no measured shelf-stacking rate fetched (van Zelst et al. 2009 IJPE doi:10.1016/j.ijpe.2006.06.010 models it but is paywalled). 45/h is ~80 s per case including walking from cage to shelf.

restock_trigger_fill.source: assumption: restocker queues a SKU when shelf fill drops below 25%; priority = P(OOS before next pass) * demand rate. Gruen & Corsten 2008 Pattern 2/4 ('check the stock more frequently ... multiple times during the day') motivates frequency, not the threshold.

backroom_dwell_hours.source: Reiner, G., Teller, C. & Kotzab, H. (2013) 'Analyzing the Efficient Execution of In-Store Logistics Processes in Grocery Retailing: The Case of Dairy Products', Production and Operations Management 22(4), doi:10.1111/poms.12003; survey of 202 stores of one central-European chain; green OA copy https://openresearch.surrey.ac.uk/view/delivery/44SUR_INST/12138884720002346/13140556810002346 (Table 3) ('stored there for an average of 12.5 hours (sigma 13)')

reorder_point_formula.value: ROP = E(L)*E(D) + SS; SS = z*sqrt(E(L)*sigma_D^2 + E(D)^2*sigma_L^2)
reorder_point_formula.source: Wikipedia 'Safety stock' https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safety_stock citing Ballou, Business Logistics/Supply Chain Management 5th ed., and Chopra, Reinhardt & Dada (2004) 'The Effect of Lead Time Uncertainty on Safety Stocks', Decision Sciences 35(1)

service_level_z.source: Wikipedia 'Safety stock' https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safety_stock citing Ballou, Business Logistics/Supply Chain Management 5th ed., and Chopra, Reinhardt & Dada (2004) 'The Effect of Lead Time Uncertainty on Safety Stocks', Decision Sciences 35(1) ('z = 1.65 for 95% service level'); range = 90%-99%.
service_level_z.note: 95% target is an assumption; the 8.3% observed OOS rate implies real stores run near ~92% availability.

lead_time_days_chilled.source: Reiner, G., Teller, C. & Kotzab, H. (2013) 'Analyzing the Efficient Execution of In-Store Logistics Processes in Grocery Retailing: The Case of Dairy Products', Production and Operations Management 22(4), doi:10.1111/poms.12003; survey of 202 stores of one central-European chain; green OA copy https://openresearch.surrey.ac.uk/view/delivery/44SUR_INST/12138884720002346/13140556810002346 (Table 3): dairy 'delivered daily to all stores', 5.9 orders/week, ordering 38.2 min/day; their simulation delivers at 6 a.m. next day and Saturday orders on Monday.

lead_time_days_ambient.source: assumption: ambient lines ride the same daily DC network but on a less frequent per-line schedule; set 2 days. No UK ambient lead-time figure fetched.

lead_time_sd_days.source: assumption: daily DC deliveries are reliable; Reiner et al. report delivery delays as an issue but no SD.

order_review_period_days.source: Reiner, G., Teller, C. & Kotzab, H. (2013) 'Analyzing the Efficient Execution of In-Store Logistics Processes in Grocery Retailing: The Case of Dairy Products', Production and Operations Management 22(4), doi:10.1111/poms.12003; survey of 202 stores of one central-European chain; green OA copy https://openresearch.surrey.ac.uk/view/delivery/44SUR_INST/12138884720002346/13140556810002346 (Table 3) (5.9 orders/week, dairy ordered daily)

slips_share_major_injuries.unit: fraction of reported major workplace injuries
slips_share_major_injuries.source: HSE leaflet INDG225(rev2) 'Preventing slips and trips at work' (2014), https://www.hse.gov.uk/pubns/indg225.pdf: slips and trips 'cause 40 per cent of all reported major injuries' and are 'the most reported injury to members of the public'.

spill_rate_per_1000_shoppers.source: assumption: no public per-shopper spill frequency found. At 1,500 shoppers/day this is ~3 spills/day, which a single cleaner can cover. HSE INDG225 only says spills must be 'cleaned up promptly'.

spill_prob_multiplier_on_collision.unit: x base drop chance for a shopper who has just bumped another
spill_prob_multiplier_on_collision.source: assumption: links spills to crowding (store-ops idea doc). Not sourced.

cleaner_response_target_min.unit: minutes from report to cleaner arrival
cleaner_response_target_min.source: assumption: HSE INDG225 requires prompt removal ('Remove spillages promptly') but gives no time; 5 min is a typical internal target.

spill_clean_and_dry_min.unit: minutes aisle blocked after cleaner arrives
spill_clean_and_dry_min.source: assumption: mop + wet-floor sign; not sourced.

checkout_lanes_needed_example.source: derived: peak_arrivals_per_hour_example / (3600 / (staffed_fixed_s + staffed_per_item_s*mean_items)) / 0.85 target utilisation (0.85 is an assumption).
checkout_lanes_needed_example.note: All-staffed equivalent; SCO terminals replace staffed lanes at ~1:2.2 per-item speed.
